udsoncan_virtual_can.transport: udsoncan.Client over ISO-TP on python-can virtual bus

metric_definitions.request_validity: Over every send step of every generated test: the request is replayed through the rules-engine oracle in sequence (same set-up and time steps). A request counts as well-formed if (a) protocol.codec.decode_request decodes it and (b) the oracle does not reject it with a format NRC (0x11 serviceNotSupported, 0x12 subFunctionNotSupported, 0x13 incorrectMessageLengthOrInvalidFormat), unless that NRC is listed in the template's declared intended_nrcs (a deliberate malformed-request probe such as write_did_invalid_length -> 0x13). rate = well-formed / send steps. The unadjusted rate (no intent exemption) is reported alongside.
metric_definitions.expected_response_accuracy: SELF-CONSISTENCY CHECK, circular by construction (expected bytes are produced by the same oracle; reported in an appendix, not a headline). oracle: share of generated send steps whose expected response frames equal a fresh rules-engine re-run of the test (and share of whole tests with zero mismatches). simulator: share of generated tests passing on the bug-free independent simulator. gold: (1) exact overlap = generated tests whose full step sequence (requests and set-up/time steps, ignoring expected responses) is identical to a gold test; agreement = identical expected responses on every step. (2) shared-prefix overlap = every distinct send step reached by an identical step prefix from power-on in both a generated and a gold test (deduplicated by prefix); agreement = identical expected frames for that step.
metric_definitions.coverage: Number of generated tests per category (positive/negative/session/security/timing) per requirement. rate = requirements with >= 1 generated test / requirements; category_presence = categories with >= 1 test across the suite / 5.
metric_definitions.template_reuse_rate: Share of generated tests whose template_id is a registered template AND whose steps are byte-identical to a fresh instantiation of that template with the test's stored parameters (independent re-check of byte provenance).
metric_definitions.citation_validity: Share of all citations attached to generated tests for which rag.citations.citation_is_valid is true against the evaluation corpus (source+ref exists; a quote must appear verbatim and its hex identifiers must belong to the chunk).
metric_definitions.bug_detection_rate: Each catalog bug is enabled alone in a fresh simulator per test. A bug is detected if >= 1 test that passes on the clean simulator fails with the bug enabled. Tests failing on the clean simulator are reported as invalid and get no credit. rate = detected bugs / catalog bugs. Reported for the generated suite, the hand-written gold suite (baseline) and their union. The 26-bug catalog (data/bugs/bug_catalog.yaml) is IN-SAMPLE: templates v2 were added after inspecting which of these bugs v1 missed.
metric_definitions.heldout_bug_detection_rate: Same procedure as bug_detection_rate on the 12 held-out bugs in data/bugs/heldout_catalog.yaml, written by a subagent that could not see templates, gold tests, eval, LLM or agent code. HEADLINE = held-out generated-suite detection. Missed-bug reasons come from a static trigger analysis (eval/heldout.py): whether any test applies the stimulus the bug description needs; reporting only.
metric_definitions.simulator_rules_agreement: A deterministic seeded random sample (eval/agreement.py; >= 5000 requests over 60-step walks with clock advances, environment/DTC changes and computed seed/key handshakes) is sent to a bug-free SimulatedEcu and a RulesSession in lockstep. agreed = requests with byte-identical response frames; a walk stops at its first disagreement.
metric_definitions.udsoncan_virtual_can: udsoncan.Client over ISO-TP on a python-can virtual bus against the simulator: 10 03 -> 27 01 seed -> 27 02 key -> 22 0100 -> 2E 0100 50 -> 22 0100 read-back == 0x50. pass/fail (fail includes any exception, with its text); 'skipped' with --skip-can.
metric_definitions.gold_clean_pass: Gold tests passing on the bug-free simulator / gold tests.
metric_definitions.pipeline_stats: Per requirement: kept tests, dropped tests (failed validation), rejected planner choices, plan attempts (retries = attempts - 1), run status.
metric_definitions.runtime: Wall-clock seconds per evaluation phase and in total (machine dependent).
metric_definitions.target_identification: Label set = target_services U target_dids U target_routines (typed, so service 0x22 and DID 0x0022 differ). Two predicted sets: (a) 'parsed' = services U dids U routines of the ParsedRequirement returned by the pipeline; (b) 'exercised' = every SID of every send step in the requirement's generated tests, every DID named by a 0x22 (all complete pairs) or 0x2E (first pair) request, and every routine id of a 0x31 request. Exact match = predicted set equals label set; for a requirement with an empty label set (NAT-020, unsupported) exact match additionally requires zero generated tests. Micro precision / recall / F1 sum TP / FP / FN over requirements.
metric_definitions.category_recall: |required_categories n categories of the requirement's generated tests| / |required_categories|. Micro = summed numerators / summed denominators; macro = mean over requirements with >= 1 required category (NAT-020 has none and is excluded).
metric_definitions.precondition_recall: |required_preconditions n preconditions established by >= 1 generated test| / |required_preconditions|, `none` skipped (requirements whose label is `none` are excluded). 'Established' is derived statically from each test's concrete steps and oracle-expected responses (mapping below). Micro and macro as for categories.
metric_definitions.fallback: A requirement counts as fallback / produced-nothing if the pipeline status is not 'completed', or the parsed requirement has no services, DIDs or routines, or it kept zero tests. Reported with the list of ids (for NAT-020 producing nothing is the correct outcome).

precondition_mapping.default_session: a request other than 0x10 is sent while the tracked session is the default session (no session change before it, or after a reset / S3 timeout), or a positive 10 01
precondition_mapping.extended_session: a 0x10 request with sub-function 0x03 (suppress bit masked) whose expected outcome is positive
precondition_mapping.programming_session: a 0x10 request with sub-function 0x02 whose expected outcome is positive
precondition_mapping.security_level_N: a sendKey (0x27, the level's key sub-function from the spec) whose expected outcome is positive; level 0x01 -> security_level_1, 0x03 -> security_level_3
precondition_mapping.vehicle_stationary: a set_environment step with vehicle_speed_kph == 0, or a positive 0x2E write / 0x31 start of a DID / routine whose spec conditions require vehicle_stationary
precondition_mapping.nvm_fault: a set_environment step with nvm_write_fault = true
precondition_mapping.routine_started: a positive 0x31 startRoutine (sub-function 0x01) followed by at least one later send step
precondition_mapping.s3_elapsed: clock advanced by more than the active session's S3 time between two send steps

interpretation.text:
**Summary.** On the held-out TEST split (n=12), the local Qwen2.5-3B model (`ollama`, prompts frozen at B3 revision 8) does **not** beat the deterministic mock on any headline metric. It is better on parsed-target *recall*. It is worse on parsed precision, F1, exact match, category recall and precondition recall. It is equal on held-out bug detection. It is about 120× slower.

**Where ollama was better**
- **Parsed-target recall on the test split:** 0.880 against 0.560 for mock (fn 3 vs 11).
- **More exact parses on hard rows.** Ollama parsed NAT-002, NAT-006, NAT-008 and NAT-016 exactly. Mock missed DIDs or services on all four; for example, on NAT-006 and NAT-016 mock missed 0x10, 0x27 and 0x2E, because its keyword rules miss session and security services that are only implied.
- **Fewer empty runs.** Ollama had 1 fallback or empty run on the test split (NAT-012). Mock had 3 (NAT-008, NAT-017, NAT-020). Across all 20 natural rows it was 1 against 4.
- **Dev split:** ollama category recall was 72.7% against 63.6%. This split was used for tuning, so it is not evidence.

**Where ollama was worse**
- **Parsed precision collapsed:** 0.512 against 0.933 (fp 21 vs 1). So test-split parsed F1 is 0.647 against 0.700, and parsed exact match is 4/12 against 5/12.
- **Invented identifiers.** The per-requirement table shows the 3B model adding identifiers the requirement never names:
  - DID 0x0140, the example DID in the parse prompt, appears on NAT-012, NAT-014 and NAT-017;
  - 0x10, 0x27 and 0x2E appear on NAT-004, NAT-019 and NAT-020;
  - on NAT-020, which has an empty label set, ollama made 5 tests where mock correctly made none.
- **Exercised exact match:** 0/12 against 2/12; exercised F1 0.435 against 0.449.
- **Category recall:** 18/28 (64.3%) against 19/28 (67.9%).
- **Precondition recall:** 11/15 (73.3%) against 12/15 (80.0%).
- **Generated suite on the seed requirements was much smaller:** 68 tests against 171. Negative tests fell from 70 to 19, session from 21 to 7, timing from 26 to 5.
- **In-sample detection:** 21/26 against 25/26. Ollama additionally missed `routine_stop_without_start`, `dtc_clear_ignores_group`, `dtc_clear_noop` and `dtc_read_ignores_mask`.

**Where they were equal**
- **Held-out bug detection (the headline):** 3/12 for both, the same three bugs: `failed_attempts_reset_by_seed_request`, `s3_not_refreshed_by_tester_present` and `session_suppress_bit_not_masked`. Union with gold was 5/12 for both, so the 2.5× smaller ollama suite lost no held-out detection.
- **Quality checks:** request validity, clean-simulator pass rate and citation validity were 100% in both modes (ollama 335/335 citations, mock 774/774).
- **Byte provenance** passed for every generated test: 158/158 ollama, 343/343 mock.
- **Retries:** no JSON or schema failures, no LLM retries and no re-plans in either mode.

**Validation evidence**
- Ollama had 10 planner choices rejected; mock had 0.
- All 10 were template ids not in the catalog:
  - invented names: `write_did_positive` (REQ-004, NAT-007) and `write_readonly_did_negative` (REQ-001);
  - the known B3 failure of copying the "(category)" suffix into `template_id`, such as `read_did_positive (positive)`. On NAT-012 all four choices were rejected this way, which produced the run's only zero-test requirement.
- The validator caught every one of these, so no invalid test was kept.

**Effect of the 4096-token context budget**
- No prompt was truncated in either mode (0 truncation events, 0 fallback-to-mock events).
- The cost is the shortlist: at most 24 options and at most 4 per template, against the full 154-option catalog the mock plans from.
- The rev-8 instruction asks for selective plans, so ollama kept 3–6 tests per seed requirement against mock's 5–18.
- This explains the lower negative, timing and in-sample coverage. For example, the DTC-clear and routine-stop bugs need template options that a short, selective plan did not choose.
- The same selectivity did not cost held-out detection on this 12-bug catalog.

**Latency**
- Wall-clock time per requirement was 30.8 s mean and 43.4 s p95 for ollama, against 0.25 s mean and 0.45 s p95 for mock. The maximum was 49.4 s.
- The ollama total was about 18 minutes for 35 requirements.
- Explain dominates, at 19.4 s mean per requirement (one LLM call per kept test). Plan takes 7.0 s and parse 4.2 s. Retrieval, instantiation and validation stay under 10 ms.

**Caveats**
- **Small sample.** The test split has n=12, and one requirement moves exact match by 8.3 points and recall noticeably.
- **GPU nondeterminism.** B3 measured about ±0.05 F1 between identical runs. The test-split F1 gap (0.647 vs 0.700, Δ = 0.053) is therefore at the edge of noise. Dev parsed F1 reproduced B3's 0.683 exactly in this run.
- **Little tuning data.** The prompts were tuned on only 8 dev rows, so overfitting to them is plausible; dev exact match was 1/8, the same as in B3.
- **Not compared against the gold tests or a larger model.** The mock's keyword rules were also written by the same author who labelled the requirements, which favours mock on precision.

**Conclusion.** With a 3B model at a 4096-token context, the LLM path is viable and safe: every byte comes from templates, and the validator caught every bad choice. It is not yet better than the rule-based mock. The clearest next steps are stripping the "(category)" suffix before validation (deferred in [PB-B3-RISK]) and suppressing the copied example DID 0x0140.
